// econ conductor tier (S1.1): The conductor is a mid-size (~30B) non-thinking OSS model that handles
every turn by default. It is cost-efficient (~100-200x cheaper than frontier
models) and keeps the prompt cache warm across turns.
A live run requires OPENROUTER_API_KEY to be set.
// econ small_model (S8.3): Cheap stateless model for incidental tasks (title generation, summaries).
Pinned to the executor tier so housekeeping never pays conductor/oracle rates.

conductor.description: econ default conductor: mid-tier OSS model for everyday coding turns (S1.1)

oracle.description: econ oracle tier: frontier reasoning model for high-risk turns (S3.2, escalateAbove=70)

reasoner.description: econ reasoner tier: mid-size thinking model for hard steps needing CoT (S3.7); placeholder — swap for any Qwen3-thinking or DeepSeek-R1-distill variant on OpenRouter

executor.description: econ executor tier: cheap ~9B stateless tool-caller for delegable executor-tier specialists — recon/lint/docstrings (S4.1); spawned per-task via the task tool, returns a digest. Placeholder — swap for any small (~7-9B) tool-calling OSS model on OpenRouter.

// econ safe permission defaults (S8.3 h: Hardened defaults: read-only tools are allowed; mutating, network, and
out-of-project actions require confirmation or are denied. Precedence is
last-match-wins (findLast in src/permission/index.ts), so the bash wildcard
is first and the specific deny patterns that override it come after.
Loosen per-project as trust is established.
// econ in-region inference + data resid: Real in-region (India) OSS endpoints are not yet provisioned; this is the
scaffolding contract. To route a tier to in-region infra, add a provider
below pointing at the India gateway (OpenAI-compatible), e.g.:
then point the tier's agent model at "econ-in/<model>". The per-tier
fallback chain + data-residency policy lives in
// econ model fallback (S8.3): Fallback is expressed config-first: each tier's ordered endpoint chain is held
in region.ts (in-region preferred, global OpenRouter as fallback). OpenCode has
no native per-model failover field, so runtime auto-failover on a 5xx is a GATED
minimal wrapper (documented in docs/sprint8/harden.md) — we did NOT modify
model.ts/router.ts. The safe always-available baseline today is the openrouter
provider above; small_model is pinned so housekeeping degrades cheaply.
